page.layout: One printed page. Page number at the head. One column of running text, set in roman and italic, with Syriac words and lines inserted in the text block. No marginal notes, no running head, no catchword.

main_text.p: stat ex ipsa definitione, seu descriptione ipsius [illegible, ~3 letters] Sciul, quam affert Hebed-iesu Chaldæus in suo libro inscripto: [illegible, ~6 letters] De Ordinatione, seu dispositione Iudiciorum, qui est collectio Canonum, & Constitutionum Ecclesiæ Nestorianorum, cap. de [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~24 letters] [illegible, ~22 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
Explicatione vocabulorum, quorum cognitio utilis, & necessaria est omnibus Christianis, præsertim ordini Sacerdotum; Ubi sic illud nomen definit: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~14 letters]

Sciul est domus Carceris tristis animarum imbecillium, seu coinquinatarum. A quo autem loco statim contradistinguit Gehennam, locum Damnatorum, ratione durationis, sic definiens: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: The Syriac (Nestorian script) is not legible enough on this scan to copy letter by letter, so each Syriac word or line is marked illegible with an estimated letter count. The Syriac lines are quotations of the definition of "Sciul" (Sheol) and "Gehenna" and are not transcribed. The first line of the page continues from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". Printed spelling kept: "Hebed-" and "iesu" split across the line end, the long s rendered as s, and the initial letter of the first line ("ftat") is a damaged "s" from the start of the word "stat".
